job:
Follow-up on the 432 Hz app (this folder, branch agent/432hz-app). Jason tested your last build on his Galaxy Note10+ (Android 12, One UI). The crash fix works, and a 4-minute FLAC fits in memory (about 225 MB RSS, no out-of-memory error). Two real-device problems came up, plus a tuning-detection improvement. Commit locally when done. Do NOT push and do NOT install anything on a phone.

On-device evidence (from logcat over adb):
- Jason pressed Convert, then left the app (Back or app switch) around 21:50. The Activity was destroyed. When he reopened it, the new screen showed "No file chosen", but the old viewModelScope job kept decoding, shifting and encoding unseen in the background (AAC encoder started 21:50:40).
- At 21:52:20, Samsung's FreecessController froze the app because it was in the background ("com.agent.audio432(state: Freezeable -> Frozen, Reason: uidIdle)", "FZ ... reason: Bg"). At that exact moment cache/converted.m4a stopped growing at 7.7 MB. It was never finalised (no moov box) and never saved to Downloads.

Tasks:
(1) Run the conversion (decode, shift, encode, save) in a foreground service with a progress notification, so it finishes when the app is in the background or the screen locks.
 - Target API 34: declare the right foregroundServiceType (mediaProcessing is the natural fit; check it's available for your compileSdk/targetSdk, otherwise use dataSync) plus the matching FOREGROUND_SERVICE and FOREGROUND_SERVICE_<TYPE> permissions.
 - Handle POST_NOTIFICATIONS at runtime on API 33+. Conversion must still work if the user denies it.
 - Hold a partial wake lock while converting. Stop the service and release the wake lock when the conversion finishes or fails.
 - Make sure the encoder always finalises the file: call MediaMuxer.stop() before release() on success, and delete partial temp files on failure.
(2) When the Activity is recreated or reopened during or after a conversion, show the current progress, or the result and player, again. Hold the state in the service (or a process-level holder or repository the ViewModel observes), not only in an Activity-scoped ViewModel. Pressing Back must not lose a running conversion.
(3) Tuning detection improvements:
 - Show the best guess even when confidence is low, e.g. "Tuning unclear: best guess A≈441.0 Hz (confidence 0.18), using 440", with a tap or button to use the guess.
 - Ignore low bass and drum content: focus on about 200-2000 Hz and favour peaks that persist across several consecutive frames (sustained notes) over one-off transients.
 - Real-device data point: a hip-hop FLAC (heavy 808 bass, rap vocals) gave confidence 0.18 with the current detector. Keep the synthetic 432/440/444 tests passing, and add a test with a synthetic mix of tuned sustained tones plus noise or percussive bursts and a sliding low-frequency tone, so the new filtering is exercised.
(4) Keep all existing unit tests green, add tests where practical, run ./gradlew test and ./gradlew assembleDebug, update AGENT_REPORT.md (what changed, test results, what still needs on-device checking), and commit locally. Do not push. Do not install on a phone.
